## Justified revision and the current sufficiency limit

7 October 2026. The [whole-continuation round](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/WHOLE-CONTINUATION-WARRANT-INTEGRATION.md) integrates an affirmative argument, substantive counterreview and two primary-source comparisons. Its bounded advance concerns what it means for an ethical judgment to change within the same whole. Actual relief or fulfillment, a changed realization, justified bearing of a retained burden, a legitimate limit on inquiry or decision, and correction of a mistaken ethical appraisal have different grounds. They are not an exhaustive taxonomy. Erasing a complaint establishes none of them; preserving a described condition does not make the old appraisal infallible.

This refines the candidate preservation requirement: allow warranted correction while retaining accountability to the actual grounds, rather than require every current verdict to remain fixed. It does not establish an unlimited duty of review, a universal priority for recovery, or a duty to preserve every activity. Finite achievement, consent, justified finality, nonproductive self-good and nonreflective affected lives remain within the whole comparison. The scope and costs of any implementation must themselves be justified.

The universal inference remains: why does a response's favorable whole realization give any intelligence with the specified actual opportunity some practical reason, independently of assent or adopted role? The candidate grounds that favor in the response–realization relationship itself. The strongest rival agrees about favorable quality and permitted effective access but treats formed responsibility as constitutive of practical favor. Its appeal to protected authority over undertakings can support permission to decline more readily than the absence of every reason. Yet the candidate still needs to establish why its proposed ground is sufficient. Neither side wins by defining “good,” “eligible” or “responsible” through the desired conclusion.

The final audit identifies this as the inherited [constitutive-answer frontier](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONSTITUTIVE-ANSWER-INTEGRATION.md), not a new universal derivation. Removing costs or prior commitments and redescribing the opportunity does not add an inference. Further work needs an independently defended constitutive explanation of sufficiency, a substantive failure in the rival's exclusive role dependence, or a discriminating correction of the ethical identification. This is the present argument's limit, not a proof that universal grounding is impossible.
